geometry_edits.rationale: Align public threshold to the verified access edge.
Emphasize an active ground condition at the access edge.
Make the split-wing void more usable and legible.
Calm the upper massing while preserving the dominant gesture.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent split-wing mass across all views, so it clears the basic coherence gate and aligns reasonably with the neighborhood-living brief. The dominant gesture is legible and the central void/cut gives a usable public figure, especially in plan. The blue access edge is acknowledged only indirectly: there is some opening and bridge-like articulation, but the response is not strongly read as a clearly public threshold aligned to the verified frontage. The silhouette is more boxy than sectional or profiled, with stepped/raised bits that feel secondary rather than program-bearing, so the section-program relationship is only moderate. No obvious view-to-view collision issues are apparent, and the parcel response is contained and oriented without merely filling a rectangle. Overall it is a plausible early massing but would benefit from a stronger access-facing carve or notch and a cleaner, more intentional section/roof move.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/community-center in scale and complexity; do not copy the larger multi-wing dispersion literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise spread with a central open court and connecting wings; good precedent for a compact neighborhood mass with legible communal void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a smaller single-volume hospitality object; transfer the entry seam and canopy logic, not the full typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple pavilion-like ground response with a clear public threshold and calm roof datum; useful for access-edge articulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate should not become a large ramped megablock; transfer the sectional relationship selectively.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Sectional terracing and a courtyard-like void can support neighborhood living when the ground edge remains active.

warnings: Plan and oblique views suggest a coherent split-wing figure, but the access response is muted compared with the strength of the central void.
The form risks reading as a generic low extrusion with rooftop fragments unless the public threshold is sharpened.
Sectional expression is present only weakly; the mass does not yet strongly communicate a lived-in upper/ground relationship.
